title: Transferred Kan model structure on algebras over a many-sorted theory
statement: Fix a universe and a small set $S$. An $S$-sorted algebraic theory $T$ is a small category with specified finite products and distinguished objects $T_s$ for $s\in S$, such that every object is a finite product of these objects, including the empty product. A strict simplicial $T$-algebra is a finite-product-preserving functor $T\to\mathrm{sSet}$, and a map is a natural transformation. Use simplicial sets, boundaries, horns, weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] and [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For every $s$, evaluation $U_s(A)=A(T_s)$ has a left adjoint $F_s$, characterized by $\operatorname{Hom}(F_sK,A)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K,U_sA)$ naturally in $K,A$. The category of strict simplicial $T$-algebras admits a cofibrantly generated model structure with weak equivalences and fibrations detected by every $U_s$. Its generating cofibrations are $F_s(\partial\Delta^n)\to F_s(\Delta^n)$ for $s\in S$, $n\geq0$, and its generating trivial cofibrations are $F_s(\Lambda_i^n)\to F_s(\Delta^n)$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. The two generating families admit functorial small-object factorizations, and cofibrations are exactly retracts of relative generating-cofibration cell maps. Here a relative cell map is a transfinite composite, continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of coproducts of generating maps. A model structure means a complete and cocomplete category with retract-closed weak equivalences satisfying two-out-of-three, and weak factorization systems (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations); trivial means also a weak equivalence, and the factorizations can be chosen functorially. In a weak factorization system each map factors as a left-class map followed by a right-class map, and each class consists exactly of maps with the corresponding lifting property against the other class.
